title: Functorial inverse-image section diagram over an under category
statement: Let $J$ be a small category and $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $j$ let $P_j$ be a precoverage and write $T_j$ for its generated Grothendieck topology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Assume every transition functor $F(a)$ is continuous for these topologies. Fix $i\in J$ and $U\in F(i)$. There exist a functor $L:\mathrm{Sh}(T_i,\mathrm{Set})\to(\mathrm{Under}(i)\to\mathrm{Set})$, natural isomorphisms $E_t:L(-)(t)\cong(F(t.hom)_s(-))(F(t.hom)U)$, and natural transformations $\theta_b:F(t.hom)_s\to F(b.right)^s\circ F(t\prime.hom)_s$ (in diagrammatic Lean notation: the latter inverse image followed by restriction), for every $b:t\to t\prime$. For every sheaf $G$ and $X\in F(i)$, the unit at $t$ followed by $\theta_b(G)$ evaluated at $F(t.hom)X$ equals the unit at $t\prime$ as an equality of arrow objects. Moreover, $E_t(G)$ followed by $\theta_b(G)$ evaluated at $F(t.hom)U$ equals $L(G)(b)$ followed by $E_{t\prime}(G)$, again as an equality of arrow objects. Here inverse image and restriction are the adjoint sheaf functors of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. No filteredness, cocone, cover-preservation, finite-limit, or colimit hypothesis or conclusion is imposed.

proof.text: For t in Under(i), set S_t(G) to sections of the inverse image along F(t.hom) evaluated at F(t.hom)(U). For a refinement b:t→t′, transpose the unit at t′ through the adjunction at t. The equation t.hom ≫ b.right = t′.hom identifies the iterated restriction functor, yielding the natural transformation theta_b and its unit equation. Naturality of the adjunction hom equivalence makes theta_b natural in G.

For an identity refinement the identity transformation and theta have the same adjunct, so injectivity gives equality. For composable refinements, compose their transposes after restriction; its adjunct is the unit at the final stage, also the adjunct of the transpose for the composite. Thus these maps agree. Evaluate at the transported U and transport along F.map_id and F.map_comp to obtain identity and composition of section maps. These maps, natural in G, define L. The natural isomorphisms E identify its evaluations with S_t; the section-map equation is this construction written in Arrow to retain endpoint transports.

theorem colimit_site_stage_section_diagram
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (P : ∀ j : J, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    (i : J) (U : F.obj i) :
    ∃ (L : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck (Type u) ⥤ (Under i ⥤ Type u))
      (E : ∀ t : Under i, L ⋙ (evaluation (Under i) (Type u)).obj t ≅
        sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck ⋙
          sheafToPresheaf (P t.right).toGrothendieck (Type u) ⋙
          (evaluation (F.obj t.right)ᵒᵖ (Type u)).obj
            (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))
      (θ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
        sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck ⟶
        sheafPullback (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck ⋙
          (F.map b.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
            (P t.right).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck),
      (∀ (G : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck (Type u))
        (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t') (X : F.obj i),
        Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app
            (op X) ≫ ((θ t t' b).app G).hom.app
              (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
        Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app
            (op X))) ∧
      ∀ (G : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck (Type u))
        (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
        Arrow.mk ((E t).hom.app G ≫ ((θ t t' b).app G).hom.app
          (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))) =
        Arrow.mk ((L.obj G).map b ≫ (E t').hom.app G)
